subject: Rivermark MAP — throughput profile, TTFT gating, concurrency carve-out
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood-inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivermark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rivermark MAP — throughput profile, TTFT gating, concurrency carve-out

Hi Daniel / Rivermark team,

Thanks again for the sync today. Per our conversation I put together a concise MAP entry that spells out the performance benchmarking scope we agreed on so we can lock the acceptance criteria and close timeline. Key ask: can you confirm the three workload slices below and the success gates (TTFT, p95 latency, and sustained concurrency) so we can book cluster time next week?

Brief summary (attached: rivermark_map_scope_v1.xlsx):
- Workload A (interactive): 8k token prompts, short continuations — target TTFT \u003c= 600ms for 90% of requests, p95 latency \u003c= 900ms, concurrency target 50 sustained RPS.
- Workload B (batch inference): 1k prompts batched into groups of 16 — throughput target 12k tokens/sec, median latency per-batch \u003c= 1.2s.
- Workload C (mixed burst): session-based multi-turn traces — target stable KV-cache hit rate \u003e= 85%, and tail TTFT impact \u003c= +20% vs cold.

Acceptance gating (proposed):
- Canary window (2 hours) to validate routing and warm caches.
- Full run: 3x 30-minute steady-state windows at target concurrency.
- Regression threshold: no more than 5% of requests past the p95 SLO vs baseline.

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm scope by EOD Mon 1/19 -> we lock run slots 1/20-1/22.
- Redwood provides run reports + raw token logs within 48 hrs of completion.

Attachments: rivermark_map_scope_v1.xlsx (workload slices + metric definitions), rvm_workload_profiles.csv (example traces).

If this looks good, well create the HubSpot MAP milestone and a DocuSign SOW for the reserved cluster time.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@rivermark.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Rivermark Eng Team <eng-team@rivermark.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rivermark MAP — throughput profile, TTFT gating, concurrency carve-out

Mina,

Thanks for the clear write-up — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For Workload A, can we tighten the TTFT target to 500ms for the baseline user journeys (search + short completion)? Were sensitive to perceived latency. If 500ms requires a different model variant, note that in the run plan.
- For Workload B, batching groups of 32 would more closely mirror our nightly throughput spike. Can you indicate whether Redwoods batching engine will automatically prefer 16 vs 32 or if we need to pre-configure batch sizes?
- For the canary, we prefer the canary to execute with a production traffic mirror (10% traffic) rather than isolated synthetic traffic so we can validate routing/fallbacks.

We can confirm scope by EOD Monday as requested. Also looping in our SRE lead (ccd) for calendar hits — if we can get run slots 1/21-1/22 thatd be preferable (we have a data embargo 1/20).

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Engineering, Rivermark
daniel.park@rivermark.com

Mina / Karthik,

Quick internal note: calendar shows limited GPU availability the week of 1/20. Two approaches we can take — 1) prioritize the canary with production mirror on 1/21 and full steady-state runs on 1/22 (preferred), or 2) split runs across two smaller clusters on 1/21 to hit the throughput targets but with a slightly higher variance risk.

Operational asks for Karthik: please validate whether batching at 32 will still preserve our tokenization/padding efficiency for the model variant we plan to use. If not, propose the quantization/variant trade-off in a short bullet list so Mina can share with Rivermark.

Also recommend we prepare a one-page "map runbook" that lists exact endpoints, token-logging keys (redacted), and rollback triggers (p95 drift \u003e 10% during canary). I can draft that and attach to the HubSpot MAP.

-Marissa

Thanks Daniel — good notes. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Workload A: we can target 500ms TTFT for the search journeys if we run the latest quantized variant (v2-q4_8). Karthik: please add the expected p95 delta vs v2-fp16 in the runbook.
- Workload B: Redwood batching prefers 32 when request shapes are homogenous; I'll include both 16/32 configs in the run workbook and label the recommended default as 32 for Rivermark.
- Canary mirror: agree, we will mirror 10% prod traffic for the canary window. We will provide a rollback policy and an opt-out toggle in the routing policy.

Ive updated the attached scope file with the 500ms target and two batching configs. Proposed schedule (final):
- Canary (mirror 10%): 2026-01-21 09:00-11:00 PT
- Full runs (three steady-state windows): 2026-01-22 02:00-05:00 PT (split into three 1-hr windows)

Operational artifacts we will deliver pre-run: runbook (single-page), token-log key (masked), and the HubSpot MAP entry (RVK-2026-0042). Post-run: raw token logs + run analysis PDF within 48 hours.

Please confirm and Ill send the DocuSign SOW for the reserved cluster time.
